_comment: User-edited defaults read by RiskSkill (SYSTEM-DESIGN.md section 7). Override per-call with explicit /risk parameters when needed. account_equity has no live source in v1 -- keep this updated by hand.

consecutive_loss_throttle.reset_condition: one subsequent WIN, or explicit logged override via /risk

costs._comment: Execution costs, per venue, read by scripts/risk_model.py and by nothing else. CLAUDE.md §34 lists `fees` and `slippage` among the inputs a risk calculation MUST consider; before 2026-09-18 neither reached any live sizing path. The backtest has modelled fees since it was written (scripts/backtest-methods.py:517, `fee_R = 2 * fee_pct / dist`), so the live path was the looser of the two -- and the R:R floor it enforces was measured NET of fees (analysis-params.json project_defined.ict.min_rr._basis: 'fee 0.05 %/side'). A gross-R floor compared against net-R evidence is a floor that admits trades the evidence rejected.
costs._order_type_why: Fee depends on whether the order takes or makes liquidity, and this platform's setups differ: ICT rests a post-only GTX limit at the FVG edge (maker); WYCKOFF-BOOK sends a market order at the bar close (taker), per each method's `entry` field in docs/architecture/methods.json runner_methods. One blended number would over-charge one family and under-charge the other. (WYCKOFF, the mechanical proxy, and COMBINED were removed 2026-09-19 -- docs/audits/2026-09-19-knowledge-fidelity.md finding 6.)

futures._source: Binance USDT-M standard VIP-0 schedule, as ASSUMED by the ranking runs recorded in docs/architecture/pilot-selection.json `fee_assumed`. NOT read from the venue: no connector fetches the account's fee tier, so this is a declared assumption and scripts/tests/test_risk_model.py asserts the setups' assumptions agree with it rather than letting each setup carry its own.

mt5._source: The broker prices CFDs in the spread rather than a separate commission, so both sides carry the same assumed round-turn cost -- the 0.05 %/side the cfd ranking runs used. Same status as futures: an assumption, not a venue read.
mt5._spread_note: For a spread-priced CFD the true cost is the spread at fill, which varies by session and is not in the bridge's export. Treating it as a flat per-side percentage is an approximation that UNDERSTATES cost when the spread widens -- which is exactly around the news releases §24 already blocks.

costs._slippage_why: NOT MODELLED, and declared null rather than 0 so that nothing can mistake 'we did not model it' for 'it is zero'. The backtest says the same thing in its own docstring ('Slippage not modelled', backtest-methods.py:44). Consequence, carried on every plan risk_model.py produces: the net R:R it reports is an UPPER BOUND, and `slippage: UNKNOWN` travels with it. Filling this in requires measured fill-vs-intent data from the pilot, which is a §41 failure-learning input that does not exist yet -- inventing a number here would be worse than the honest null.

_max_risk_note: max_risk_pct is THE per-trade risk ceiling for every order path, manual and automated. One authored value, one validated reader: scripts/trading_env.py MAX_RISK_PCT (via _read_max_risk_pct, which refuses rather than guessing). Its readers are strategy-runner.RISK_CEILING, scripts/trading-env.sh (PILOT_RISK_PCT clamp), scripts/session-safety-rules.sh (the SessionStart reminder) and RiskSkill/RiskAgent -- none of them may restate the number. Unified at 0.01 on 2026-09-17 by user decision: until then this file said 0.01 while trading_env.py said 0.03, so the automated pilot sized at three times what the manual /execute path enforced and the session hook announced 3%. Express it as a FRACTION (0.01 = 1%); the reader rejects anything outside (0, 1], so a `3` typed for '3%' refuses instead of risking 300% of equity.
_max_portfolio_risk_note: THE ceiling on risk summed across EVERY account, as a FRACTION of the summed equity those accounts reported. One authored value, one validated reader: scripts/exposure.py _read_ceiling(), which refuses rather than guessing -- exactly the shape of max_risk_pct above. Why it is needed: max_risk_pct bounds one trade on one account, and nothing bounded the sum. Ten accounts each risking their own 1 % on the same BTCUSDT signal is one 10 % bet with ten tickets, and no per-account check can see that (CLAUDE.md §34 'existing exposure'; scripts/risk_model.py open_risk measures one book, not the portfolio). 0.05 is a STARTING value chosen by this change, not a measured one: it is five times the per-trade ceiling, so it admits five fully-sized concurrent positions across the whole estate before it refuses. Raise it only against measured evidence of how correlated the accounts' books actually are -- with every account on the same setups the correlation is 1.0 and the sum IS the risk. Added 2026-09-19 with docs/plans/2026-09-19-multi-account.md.
_max_correlated_accounts_note: How many accounts OF ONE OWNER may hold the same (symbol, side) at the same moment. One authored value, one validated reader: scripts/exposure.py _read_correlated_cap(), which refuses rather than guessing. This is the PRIMARY multi-account gate, and max_portfolio_risk_pct is not: a ceiling expressed as a fraction of summed equity is invariant in the number of accounts (10 accounts x $10k each risking 1 % of their own equity is 1 % of the total, and so is 100), so it cannot bound the hazard that grows with N. That hazard is SIMULTANEOUS FAILURE: each prop account carries its own daily-loss and total-drawdown limit (docs/architecture/account-profiles.json), so if every account is long the same symbol, one adverse move breaches every account's daily limit on the same day. SCOPED PER OWNER because the estate is not one person's (user, 2026-09-19): customers rent a methodology and hand over their own account. Ten accounts of one owner long the same symbol is that owner's concentrated bet, and is capped. Two different customers who both chose that methodology holding the same symbol is two people's separate decisions, and refusing the second would mean whoever's runner ticks first wins -- so the house-wide count is REPORTED on every grant (`house_holders`) and never refused on. 3 is a STARTING value chosen by this change, not a measured one. It is also a MEASUREMENT: if an owner's accounts are genuinely running different methodologies they will rarely collide and this will rarely bind, so a cap that binds constantly is evidence the 'different methodologies' premise is false. Added 2026-09-19 with docs/plans/2026-09-19-multi-account.md.
_capacity_required_above_accounts_note: Above how many accounts holding ONE symbol an undeclared instrument capacity stops being reported and starts refusing. One authored value, one validated reader: scripts/exposure.py _read_capacity_threshold(). Why it exists: the same signal across N accounts sends N orders into the same book within seconds, so on a thin instrument the estate moves the price against itself and everyone after the first few fills worse. Nothing in this repository reads order-book depth, so we CANNOT set a capacity -- and inventing one would be worse than saying so. A symbol may declare `max_estate_notional_usd` in docs/architecture/instruments.json and then it is a hard ceiling; where it does not, the grant carries capacity: UNDECLARED and the estate is allowed to stay small on that symbol. Above this count it refuses instead, because at that size trading on an unmeasured capacity assumption is the silent unknown CLAUDE.md §20 forbids. 10 is a STARTING value chosen by this change, not a measured one. Added 2026-09-19 with docs/plans/2026-09-19-multi-account.md §0.3 item 4.
